general: Before you reread, try to recall the key idea from memory. Pulling it out makes it stick.
A little study on several days beats one long cram.
Explain what you just learned in your own words, as if to a friend.
Stuck on something? Asking a mentor early saves time.
End each chapter by writing down one question you still have.
Mix up your practice. It feels harder, and that is why it works.
Take a short break every 50 minutes or so. Your focus comes back fresher.
Skim the headings before you start, so you know where the chapter is going.
Link each new idea to something you already know.
Sleep helps memory. A good night's rest is part of studying.
A missed quiz question is useful: it shows exactly what to review.
Silence notifications while you study and focus on one thing at a time.
A short note in your own words beats highlighting.
Set a small goal for today, like one chapter. Small wins add up.
